calls.summary:
# Realtime Analytics
Date: 2026-09-01 | Duration: 32m

## Summary
The discussion examined real-time analytics designed to address customer warehouse lag of 2–24 hours, with a managed warehouse providing earlier visibility and preview flags for major experiment issues. Tracking plugins can bifurcate events so exposures reach both warehouses, while customers manually select warehouse metrics; advanced statistics may be excluded. ClickHouse already contains the required data, but integration must remain simple. A diagnostic feed was proposed to filter experiments, feature flags, specific user IDs, and post-exposure events, potentially with session-recording links and reusable feature-page surfaces. Real-time refreshes and opt-in historical queries were discussed, alongside possible seven-day retention and larger-window queries through customer warehouses. For sampling, the MVP may use organization-level manual rates, feature overrides, and automatic expiry for temporary increases, with scheduled sampling considered later. Customers must scrub sensitive data before transmission. A Block proposal was expected shortly, as its Amplitude contract ends in December; replacement economics target near $100K monthly. Notion also needs diagnostics visibility, and Jeremy will clarify dynamic sampling and gather customer feedback.

## Keywords
Real-time analytics, Dynamic sampling, Experiment diagnostics, Managed warehouse, ClickHouse, Feature flags

## Action Items
**Jeremy Dorn**
Finalize dynamic sampling approach (30:15)
Follow up with Block (30:15)
Send proposal document (30:25)
